author: Anthony Maenza
title: Suspect in Penn Park homicide arrested after traffic stop: York police - NewsBreak
text:
By Anthony Maenza ,
1 days ago A 17-year-old suspect in May's fatal Penn Park shooting was arrested following a traffic stop, York City police say.
Kveyon Jordan Shue was arrested on July 8 by York City Police, three months after police sought him in connection with the slaying of 15-year-old Dy Qual Harris on May 5. Shue's arrest warrant was first issued on May 8.
Harris' death led to an outpouring of grief across York City and a crackdown by police, who stepped up patrols and surveillance around the park that's situated near William Penn High School.
"Keep things quiet and keep us off your back," Police Commissioner Michael Muldrow said in May . "I challenge everybody: Keep me out of a job."
More: Blasting work to cause I-83 traffic delays in southern York County
More: Drain flies, sanitizer issues found at York County mini-market
According to court documents, Shue was apprehended by police while riding in a vehicle being driven by 18-year-old Jasani Kotek. Shue was among three passengers in the vehicle Kotek was driving.
Shue is currently being held in York County Prison without bail. A preliminary hearing for Shue is scheduled for July 28.
Around 2:55 p.m., police observed the vehicle being driven by Kotek with Shue inside in the area of South Belvidere Avenue and West Princess Street. Police followed the vehicle to the area of College Avenue and Herman Street, where they conducted a traffic stop.
After a brief alleged altercation, police say Shue was taken into custody.
Another teenager, Troy Brown Jr., of York City, is jailed as an adult, facing homicide and conspiracy charges in connection with the Penn Park homicide.

Investigators, from charging documents in Brown Jr.'s recently unsealed criminal case, alleged that Brown and Shue were associates of Parkway, that Harris was associated with Southside, and that an argument on an Instagram chat led to the shooting.
Kotek was arrested following the traffic stop and has been charged with hindering apprehension, a felony. She has also been charged with resisting arrest and obstructing justice, both misdemeanors.
According to court documents, police had talked to Kotek about Shue’s whereabouts on June 25. Police said Kotek told them that she could contact Shue through her brother and offer to give him a ride in order for police to conduct surveillance on Shue and attempt to take him into custody.
Police say they attempted to coordinate the arrest of Shue with Kotek on three different dates, but Kotek did not answer calls or texts made to her.
More: Dover man sentenced to 18 to 40 years for mother-in-law's homicide
On July 7, Kotek, police said, questioned them about a residence where they searched for Shue and Shue was nervous about being apprehended.
Kotek’s bail was set at $250,000 and currently in York County Prison.
